Now I see the issue. The `encode_frame` function doesn't validate `max_payload` against the payload length. Let me fix that.
Repaired. The bug was that `encode_frame` never checked `max_payload` against the payload length. Added a guard returning `FrameError::PayloadTooLarge` when `payload.len() > max_payload`, and replaced the lossy `payload.len() as u32` cast with `try_into().map_err(|_| FrameError::Overflow)`. All 2 tests pass and the full Holzman verification gate passes clean.

@@ -5,10 +5,16 @@

 }
 
 pub fn encode_frame(payload: &[u8], max_payload: usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FrameError> {
+    if payload.len() > max_payload {
+        return Err(FrameError::PayloadTooLarge);
+    }
     let mut out = Vec::new();
-    let len = payload.len() as u32;
+    let len: u32 = payload
+        .len()
+        .try_into()
+        .map_err(|_| FrameError::Overflow)?;
     out.extend_from_slice(&len.to_be_bytes());
     out.extend_from_slice(payload);
     Ok(out)
 }
